diagnostic_evidence.quote: and, for every $\tau\in (0,\frac{c}{2L^2})$ and $\eta$ sufficiently small

issues.failure_explanation: The proof obtains a contraction factor bounded by $1-2\tau c+2\tau^2L^2+4\sqrt{\eta}+8\eta$. The stated hypothesis quantifies over every $\tau\in(0,c/(2L^2))$. As $\tau\to0$, this bound tends to $1+4\sqrt{\eta}+8\eta>1$, so the imposed bound on $\eta$, which is independent of $\tau$, does not imply $\rho<1$ for all such $\tau$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the condition so that it ensures $1-2\tau c+2\tau^2L^2+4\sqrt{\eta}+8\eta<1$ for the chosen $\tau$, e.g. restrict $\tau$ to a subinterval bounded away from $0$ or make the small-$\eta$ bound depend on $\tau$, and adjust the theorem statement accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated linear mean-square convergence for all sufficiently small step sizes is unsupported; results relying on this theorem, in particular the complexity corollary, are affected until the step-size condition is repaired.
issues.title: Contraction condition does not rule out small step sizes
issues.why_classification: The fix is local and does not require new proof architecture, but it necessarily weakens the advertised quantifier over $\tau$; hence it is more than minor.

issues.failure_explanation: The denominator $\EE^{\mathrm{ML}}[Y_L]$ is a sample average of level differences $Y_l-Y_{l-1}$, which may be negative. Nothing in the hypotheses guarantees $\EE^{\mathrm{ML}}[Y_L]>1$ (or even positivity) for the random samples. The proof divides by this denominator and uses the lower bound $1$ without establishing it, so the mean-square inequality is not valid as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: At minimum, the proof must either add a uniform lower-bound hypothesis on $\EE^{\mathrm{ML}}[Y_L]$ (or modify the estimator with a safe denominator/truncation) and reprove the MSE and complexity estimates under that condition, or provide a nontrivial argument ensuring the denominator is bounded away from zero with high probability.
issues.overall_effect: The MSE bound for the MLMC gradient estimator, the complexity theorem that uses it, and the corollary relying on both are unreliable; the adaptive sample-based constant $\widehat C$ and the estimator itself can be ill-defined when the denominator vanishes or is too small.
issues.title: MLMC ratio denominator is not controlled
issues.why_classification: A conditional version with a lower-bound assumption is source-supported and local to the ratio argument, but the advertised unconditional estimator guarantee is lost and a contained probabilistic lower-bound argument or estimator modification is required.

issues.failure_explanation: $e_k$ is defined as $\rho^k$, i.e. the expected squared distance. The iteration count $K\sim 2\log\varepsilon/\log\rho$ gives $e_K\sim\varepsilon^2$, not $\varepsilon$. The proof then applies the gradient-estimation cost with powers $e_k^{-2}$ and claims $e_K\cong\varepsilon$, treating $e_k$ as the distance. As written, the exponents in the geometric-sum calculation do not follow from the definitions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the bookkeeping, e.g. define $e_k=\rho^{k/2}$ (distance) and target MSE $e_k^2$, or equivalently use $e_k=\rho^k$ with cost powers $e_k^{-1}$ and final $e_K\sim\varepsilon^2$, so that the sums yield the claimed exponents.
issues.overall_effect: The stated asymptotic total-cost bounds of the idealized corollary are not established by the proof, although the final rates are intended to be the standard ones.
issues.title: Complexity corollary proof mixes squared error and distance
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local notation/exponent correction that preserves the advertised final complexity rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The formula for $M_{k,\ell}^{\mathrm{opt}}$ is intended to be evaluated before the current samples are drawn, but the summand uses $v_{k,\ell'}$, which is defined from $M_{k,\ell'}$ current-sample deviations. For $\ell'\neq\ell$ (and generally) $v_{k,\ell'}$ is not available when choosing $M_{k,\ell'}$, making the batch-size determination circular. The formula also divides by $M_{k-1,\ell'}-1$ without excluding $M_{k-1,\ell'}=1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use only delayed estimates, e.g. replace $v_{k,\ell'}$ by $v_{k-1,\ell'}$ (or another available pilot estimate) in the sum, and specify a convention or constraint for $M_{k-1,\ell'}=1$.
issues.overall_effect: The adaptive algorithm's stated optimal batch allocation is not well defined as written, so its practical complexity guarantee and the online estimation scheme cannot be implemented directly from the formula.
issues.title: Optimal batch-size formula uses unavailable current-level variance estimates
issues.why_classification: A consistent indexing and a degenerate-case convention give a local repair that preserves the intended adaptive allocation.

issues.failure_explanation: If $\EE^{\text{MC}}_k[\Delta X_\ell]$ estimates the consecutive-level weak-error difference of order $C h_\ell^{\widehat\alpha}$, then the bias at the current finest level $L$ is of order $C h_L^{\widehat\alpha}=C h_\ell^{\widehat\alpha}(h_L/h_\ell)^{\widehat\alpha}$. The formula divides by $(h_L/h_\ell)^{\widehat\alpha}$, producing an estimate with the inverse mesh-ratio scaling, so it does not estimate the intended squared bias used in the level update.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the extrapolation factor so that the level-ℓ difference is multiplied by $(h_L/h_\ell)^{2\widehat\alpha}$ (or use a consistent cumulative bias estimator), and then the level update compares the intended bias to $\varepsilon_k^2/2$.
issues.overall_effect: The adaptive level update may refine or stop based on a systematically distorted bias estimate, so the algorithm's stated online error control and optimal-complexity behavior are not guaranteed.
issues.title: Squared bias estimator extrapolates with the wrong mesh ratio
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local formula fix for the bias estimator; the intended adaptive algorithm and complexity argument can be preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In other words, the distance $d = B - A$ of processes which store data to the same point

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed condition only requires all processes in $\pi_{s_{k,\ell}}(x)$ to lie in one residue class modulo $P_{s_{k,\ell}}$. It does not require that residue class to contain the world-communicator process $\pi_0(x)$. For example, with $P_s=4$, $\pi_s(x)=\{1,5,9,13\}$ satisfies the congruence condition, but $\pi_0(x)=\{0\}$ is not a subset. Hence the claimed communication-free selection and the algorithm's no-error check do not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the condition to require every process in $\pi_{s_{k,\ell}}(x)$ to be congruent to the unique process in $\pi_0(x)$ modulo $P_{s_{k,\ell}}$ (equivalently, enforce $\pi_0(x)\subseteq\pi_{s_{k,\ell}}(x)$), and adjust the domain-decomposition discussion accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The parallel data-merging algorithm's guarantee that $\texttt{SelectSubdomain}$ can operate without additional communication or an error is unsupported for domain decompositions satisfying only the stated congruence condition.
issues.title: Congruence condition does not guarantee nested process sets
issues.why_classification: A local strengthening of the congruence/alignment condition preserves the intended communication-free update without changing the mathematical method.
